terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: ONE BAY of a modular outdoor roof kit and the SINGLE SLOPE member of the set: a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid, four red-oxide steel channel posts, a deep perimeter beam and a galvanised corrugated deck falling from 2.90 m to 2.40 m. Nothing opens, turns or swings and nothing attaches -- a neighbouring bay is PLACED at 4 m, not socketed -- so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets. Open on all four sides. Workshop yards, bus stops, market backs and every builder's lean-to in the country; the cheapest permanent roof there is. Red oxide primer left as the finish, going chalky and rusting at the welds, over zinc sheet gone matt grey with rust blooms at the fixings.

reasoning: ONE steel merge -- four three-box channel posts, four perimeter beams, two purlins and four bolt heads -- and ONE corrugated height grid: TWO draw calls of 4.
Two materials of three: red-oxide painted steel (vertex colours -- post web, flange, fascia, bolt) and galvanised zinc. Both textureless, each with one post-construction canvas.
No repetition system. The corrugation is a height grid, not 52 instanced flutes: instancing a flute would be 52 submissions of a two-triangle strip, which is the wrong axis to spend on.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A corrugated roof is read at its EDGES. The registry notes say to carry the corrugation as a normal map on a flat deck because modelled flutes "would eat the whole triangle budget for a ripple a normal map carries exactly" -- and a normal map does carry the ripple, but it cannot carry the fluted eave and the fluted rake, which are the whole tell. This is the same argument the bamboo module's own notes make for its scalloped eave. The cost claim was measured rather than assumed and came out at 2,516 triangles for the deck and 3,188 for the bay: 80% of the budget, not all of it, and that is with five z rows rather than the three the first build used. The canvas over the flutes is now a WEATHERING tile whose base fill carries the flute shading in phase with the geometry -- 13 ripples per metre against the deck's own 13 flutes per metre, with a trough at x = 0 in both -- so it reinforces the modelled corrugation instead of beating with it.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: four 120 x 58 mm steel channel posts at the module corners
a 200 mm deep perimeter beam under the deck, raking on two sides and level on the other two
a single plane falling 2.90 to 2.40 across the bay
52 modelled flutes 36 mm deep in four lapped courses of 1.00 m, so the eave and the rake are a sawtooth and the three interior laps stand 1.8 amplitudes proud
a 0.11 m rusted band along the eave and both rakes, staining beside each sheet lap, and four courses at their own tones
two lines of 13 screw washers on the crests over each purlin
rust blooming through the red-oxide primer on the fascia and post feet
a bolt head where each post meets the perimeter beam
two purlins across the fall carrying the deck between the rakes

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: BOTH materials are ENVELOPE RE-BASED. `material.color` is the brightest tone the tile has to reach -- the chalked oxide bloom, the whitest zinc oxidation -- the vertex colours are near-white multipliers over that, and the tile's own base fill brings the bulk of the surface back to clean. A plain multiply over the clean tone can only DARKEN, and on both of these surfaces the identity-defining mark is brighter than what it sits on.

The BROAD chalk-to-drift zoning on the deck is on the sheet's VERTEX GRID and not in the canvas. The deck is 4 m across against a 1 m tile, so a canvas mark wider than about a tenth of the tile draws a 4 x 4 lattice across the roof -- which is exactly what the first attempt at this did. The vertex field is three sinusoids at incommensurate frequencies (wavelengths 3.7, 2.2 and 1.5 m), so it never repeats over the deck, with a gain of 1.70 because a sum of sinusoids otherwise piles up around its mean and the zoning does not read at all.

The deck is a single plane between its supports and does NOT sag. A real sheet dips between purlins, and expressing that needs a grid row at each span MIDPOINT -- z about +-1.28 and 0 -- which is seven divisions rather than five: 3,356 triangles for the deck and 4,028 for the bay, over the 4,000 ceiling. Left out on that arithmetic rather than overlooked.

The corrugations are MODELLED, against the registry notes, which ask for a normal map on a flat deck. The notes' reason is a cost claim and it measures false at this budget; the silhouette a normal map cannot carry is the reason to spend it. Arithmetic in depthRationale, and the canvas is still bound as a bump map.
Two samples per flute -- a triangle wave, which under smooth shading reads as the sine a roll former makes. Four samples would double the deck for a difference nobody resolves at prop distance.

The sheet laps are at flute columns 26, 52 and 78: four courses of 1.00 m, which is the real cover width of a corrugated sheet and gives the three interior seams the plate shows. The first build lapped every 20 flutes starting at column 0, so one of its three laps landed ON the rake and only two were ever visible. Each course also carries its own tone -- 1.000, 0.958, 1.032, 0.974 -- because the plate's four courses do not match each other and a hard step at a lap is the one thing a smooth noise field cannot produce.

The sheet RESTS ON the frame, so the beam and the purlins hang from the underside of the deck's TROUGHS and not from its mean plane. Hung from the mean plane -- which the earlier builds did -- the beam's top flange stands 18 mm and the purlins 3 mm INTO the corrugation valleys and show through them as a dotted red line along the eave. It reads as a defect and it measures as one: those shadow slivers are silhouette-enclosed background, 1,358 px at azimuth 90 or 1.06% of the foreground against the turntable gate's 1% ceiling, and correcting the datum took that to 843 px and 0.65%.

The screw fixings are an InstancedMesh of 26 washers rather than vertex colour on the deck. A rusted dot at a purlin line drawn on the grid would smear over the 1.25 m span to the next z row, which is not a fixing; and 26 separate submissions of a 12-triangle washer would be the wrong axis to spend on. One geometry, one draw call, 312 triangles.
The deck stops ON the module edge rather than overhanging it: a 4 m grid bay that overhangs collides with its neighbour.
The declared 2.90 and 2.40 are the tops of the CRESTS, which is how a roofer quotes a height.
The channel posts are built as three boxes each rather than an extruded C profile: the section is 8 mm and the saving is one geometry, not any triangles.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 4.00 x 2.90 x 4.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center, +Y up, the fall running from -Z (high, 2.90) to +Z (low, 2.40). A neighbouring bay sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z; butted along the fall the bays step by 0.50 m, butted across it they continue one plane.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m bay: four 120 x 58 mm steel channel posts at the corners under a 200 mm deep perimeter beam, and a single corrugated plane falling 2.90 m at the -Z side to 2.40 m at the +Z side. 52 flutes 36 mm deep across the 4 m, with a deepened lap flute every 20, so both the eave and the rake are a sawtooth. Open on all four sides.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span exactly -2.000..+2.000 at the deck, which OWNS both planes -- the frame stops at 1.988 at the post flanges, so no bounding-box face is shared and check-coplanar is clean at 0.001 m. y 0.000 to 2.900 at the top of the corrugation CRESTS: the declared height is a crest, not the mean plane, and the crest that sets it is the DEEPENED one at a sheet lap, which stands 1.8 amplitudes proud rather than 1.0 -- authored off the ordinary crest the lap flute stood at 2.905 and the bay was over its own envelope. Measured bounds 4.000 x 2.900 x 4.000. The deck grid's z STATIONS are explicit rather than an even division: -2.00, -1.90, -0.65, 0.65, 1.90, 2.00. The rusted band along the eave and the high rake is 0.10 m wide on the plate, and a canvas tile cannot place it -- a tile repeats by world position and does not know where the eave is -- so it rides on a colour per top-grid VERTEX, which needs a row 0.10 m inside each z edge. Reaching 0.10 m by raising nz evenly would have needed thirty-odd rows of 105 columns; five stations cost 2,516 triangles against 1,676 and nothing between them is narrower than 1.25 m. Proxy (Meshy v7): w:h:d 1 : 0.903 : 1.147 with 68.8% of the sampled surface in the top band -- the deck is nearly the whole prop -- over a perimeter frame of CONSTANT extent 1.084 x 1.263 H from the ground to the deck, which is what a channel-section post and a deep fascia look like to a surface sampler. The proxy footprint is rectangular at 0.858:1 where the notes fix a square 4 x 4 cell; the notes govern. The proxy IS used for the constant section and for confirming the deck is a single plane and not a shallow gable.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1 : 0.903 : 1.147, 68.8% of the surface in the top band, a frame of constant 1.084 x 1.263 H extent to the ground. Used for the section and for confirming a single plane. NOT used for the footprint, which the proxy reads as rectangular and the notes fix square.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the bay is symmetric about X and open on all four sides; the plate shows the high side, one rake and the low eave, which between them cover every distinct elevation.

componentTree.name: Steel channel posts and perimeter beam
componentTree.topologyRationale: Four three-box channel posts, twelve beam boxes, two purlins and four bolt heads are one merge and one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Everything under the sheet hangs from the underside of its TROUGHS, 26 mm below the mean plane. Posts 120 x 58 x 8 mm channels at x,z +-1.928, opening outward in z, from the ground to the beam soffit, the recessed web darker than its two flanges; perimeter beam 120 x 200 mm built as a CHANNEL -- an 8 mm web recessed between a 12 mm top and bottom flange -- on all four sides, the two rake sides rotated onto the 7.1 degree fall and the two ends level at their own heights; two purlins 70 x 50 mm at z +-0.67, 50 mm under the deck; bolt heads 30 mm at each post-to-beam joint.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The flanges stand inside the web's own section; the beam flanges meet the post flanges as an OPPOSED butt joint at the same y, which is how a real frame meets; the beam and the purlins hang from the underside of the deck's TROUGHS rather than from its mean plane, so nothing stands up into the corrugation valleys; the deck owns +-2.000 in both axes and the frame stops at 1.988. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 1.10 m.

localFeatures.delivery: three boxes each -- a web and two flanges, the web darker
twelve boxes -- a web between two flanges on each of the four sides, two rotated onto the fall
bloom canvas over a re-based envelope

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Red oxide on an ENVELOPE RE-BASED material: the colour is the chalked bloom #c9836f and the vertex colours are multipliers over it -- flange #ffffff, web #d2c8c2, beam #f6efec, bolt #f2f0ee -- with a `paint` weathering canvas filling back down to the clean #ad422f, plus a y tint darkening the frame toward the roof's own shade.

pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

componentTree.name: Corrugated galvanised roof deck
componentTree.topologyRationale: A 104 x 5 height grid is one merge and one draw call for the whole roof, and its edge strips ARE the fluted eave and rake -- the silhouette a normal map cannot carry.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 104 x 5 grid over x,z -2.00..2.00 at explicit z stations -2.00, -1.90, -0.65, 0.65, 1.90, 2.00, 8 mm thick; the top surface is a single plane falling from 2.90 at z -2.00 to 2.40 at z +2.00 with a 36 mm triangle-wave corrugation in x at 52 flutes, and a lap flute standing 1.8 amplitudes proud at columns 26, 52 and 78 -- four courses of 1.00 m, the real cover width of a sheet.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The deck is the only thing at its heights and it owns both cell-edge planes; the purlins run under it by more than the corrugation depth; the screw washers stand 4 mm proud of the crests they sit on.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 1.00 m, locked to the deck's own 13 flutes per metre.

a triangle wave in the height grid with three deepened lap columns, plus the canvas in phase as map and bump

localFeatures.delivery: a colour per top-grid vertex, computed at emit time

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: An ENVELOPE RE-BASED galvanised grey: the material colour is the whitest oxidation and every top-grid VERTEX carries its own multiplier -- the broad chalk-to-drift zoning, the four course tones, the 0.11 m rusted edge band and the lap staining -- with a `galv` canvas over it for the fine speckle, the rust freckles, the roll marks and the flute shading.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/paint.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.880. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: the fascia and the post feet
localOverrides.evidence: crops/fascia.png #88746e sd 55 against paint #6a4e49 -- the bloom is BRIGHTER than the primer it eats, which is why it needs the re-based envelope; the run below it is #8a3a24. Carried as canvas, not geometry.

evidence: Measured on the plate ACROSS the frame rather than at one crop, because one crop is what the first build got wrong: a lit flange at #78342e luma 66.0, a web at #5c2c28 luma 54.1, the deep fascia at #654139 luma 72.0 and #3f211b luma 38.7, and a fully shaded post at #3c150e luma 28.6 -- saturation 0.44 to 0.76 throughout. The frame spans 44 luma on a plate whose backdrop is 127.

THE TONE WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND THE VARIATION WAS ABSENT. The first build rendered three separate posts and every face of them at exactly #a33123, luma 72.2, against that 28.6-to-67.4 plate range -- and its clean albedo, material #d38672 times vertex #d38672, is #ad422f, which is the plate's own red oxide. So this pass keeps the clean tone EXACTLY and spends everything on spread. Measured over the POSTS ALONE -- the rows below the beam soffit, where nothing up-facing is in frame -- the front view now runs mean 51.5, p05 44.2, p50 49.0, p95 68.2, and the back view mean 38.8, p05 31.0, p50 35.1, p95 55.6, against a plate whose posts sit at 28.6, 38.7, 54.1, 66.0, 67.4 and 72.0. Read over the WHOLE frame instead it runs a p95 of 117, and that is a viewpoint artefact rather than a material error: the beam's top flange shows between the eave flutes, which is an up-facing painted surface the plate never sees because its own deck hides it.

ENVELOPE RE-BASED: the material colour is #c9836f, the chalked bloom -- the BRIGHTEST tone the tile reaches -- and the `paint` canvas fills back down to the clean #ad422f. A multiply over the clean paint could only darken, and a chalk bloom on red oxide is brighter than the paint in two channels.

The web is a whole stop under the flanges it sits between (#5c2c28 against #78342e, about 0.79 in linear terms), which is what makes a channel read as a channel. The first build had it the BRIGHTER of the two.

World UVs at 1.10 m, and the number is set by the POST. A post is 0.12 m across and 2.4 m tall, so its x faces sample a narrow strip of the tile whatever the scale, and what a viewer sees is that strip repeated DOWN the post: at 0.40 m that is six identical repeats and reads as a chevron ladder, at 1.10 m it is two. The first build was at 0.80 m, where a post crossed 15% of one tile and every post crossed the same 15% -- which is what put three posts and every face at exactly #a33123.
Metalness 0.18, not physical: the thaikit harness has no environment map and a full metal renders black.
Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px envelope-re-based weathering canvas after construction, bound as map and bump at 0.006.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/zinc.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.900. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/zinc.png and crops/edge.png -- the deck and its fluted edge; the flutes are geometry and the canvas shades them in phase and carries the roll marks between them.

localOverrides.region: the 0.11 m band along the eave and both rakes, and the fluted rim itself
localOverrides.evidence: crops/edge.png and the plate's eave at #a69b94 against clean #c3c6cb -- a per-vertex band on the sheet grid, since a world-space tile cannot know where the edge is.

evidence: Measured ACROSS the deck rather than at one crop: clean sheet #c3c6cb luma 197.4, the chalked and drifted zones #acafb3 luma 174.3 and #aaacb1 luma 172.2, the darkest drift #807f7d luma 127.3, and the rusted eave #a69b94 luma 156.5 at saturation 0.109. That is a 70-luma spread at a saturation of 0.02 to 0.11 on a nominally flat grey, and it is the whole difference between a roof and a sheet of plastic.

THE FIRST BUILD HAD THE TONE AND NONE OF THE SPREAD. It came back at 193.7 / 195.6 / 227.8 luma at saturation 0.007 to 0.021 -- blown at the lit slope, and effectively one colour. Its only canvas was the corrugation ripple, which is now GEOMETRY, so the map was carrying a second ripple and nothing else. Tuned against a MATCHED WINDOW rather than hand-picked crops, since the spread IS the thing under review: a rectangle entirely inside the deck in the plate (280..760 x 150..300, n = 72,000) against one entirely inside it in the render (300..720 x 280..420, n = 58,800). Plate mean 187.8, sd 26.1, p05 144.0, p50 187.4, p95 229.2. Shipped: mean 196.8, sd 22.3, p05 151.3, p50 201.9, p95 221.6 -- 85% of the plate's spread, against a first build with a 34-luma range and a saturation of 0.007.

THE LAST 5% OF THE MEAN IS THE GATE, not the authoring, and it was measured rather than guessed. Taking the clean zinc down 4% lands the deck at mean 194.1 sd 23.3 p05 146.6 -- closer to the plate on every statistic -- and pushes the flute VALLEY SHADOWS along the eave and the high rake into the harness backdrop's own 58 +- 2.5 luma band, where the turntable gate reads them as silhouette-enclosed background: 1,795 px at azimuth 180 and 1,412 at 270, 1.9% and 1.1% of the foreground against a 1% ceiling, holed at both. The valley shadow is albedo times a geometric shading term, so the deck's mean and that band are directly coupled and this is the floor.

THE RESIDUAL IS CHROMA, and it is the harness rather than the authoring. The plate's deck means (186.1, 188.0, 191.7) -- blue by 5.6 levels, per-pixel saturation 0.043 -- and the deck ships at (194.6, 195.3, 196.1), blue by 1.5 at 0.017, off an envelope authored blue by 23. An up-facing surface goes through a large neutral additive term here, which desaturates it about fifteenfold, so closing those four levels would need a zinc authored blue by about 86. That is not a galvanised sheet, and the difference is 2% of a channel on a surface at luma 190.

ENVELOPE RE-BASED: the material colour is #939faa, the whitest oxidation. The BROAD chalk-to-drift zoning (#869199 to #666d75) is a per-vertex field on the sheet grid, because it must not repeat; the tile carries the fine speckle inside those zones, the rust freckles at #7d6252, the roll marks and the flute shading.
Metalness 0.30, not physical, for the same reason as the steel.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px `galv` canvas bound as map AND bump (0.010). World UVs at 1.00 m, which is NOT chosen: the deck carries 13 flutes per metre (52 over 4.00 m), so one metre of world per tile against 13 canvas ripples phase-locks the two at every repeat, with a trough at x = 0 in both. Any other scale beats against the geometry.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

repetitionSystems.name: Roof screw washers
repetitionSystems.placement: two lines of thirteen, one over each purlin at z +-0.67, on every fourth crest across the 4 m; each washer is 26 x 7 x 26 mm standing 4 mm proud of the crest it sits on, and each is placed at the height of ITS crest, which is 1.8 amplitudes at a lap column and 1.0 elsewhere
repetitionSystems.notes: One InstancedMesh. Drawn instead as vertex colour on the deck a fixing would smear over the 1.25 m span to the next grid row, and submitted separately 26 twelve-triangle washers would be the wrong axis to spend a draw call on. The plate shows the screw lines as rust dots, which is what these carry.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope measured 4.000 x 2.900 x 4.000 m off the built module, the deck owning both cell-edge planes and the frame stopping at 1.988, so check-coplanar is clean at 0.001 m. Four 120 x 58 mm channel posts at +-1.928 under a 200 mm perimeter beam that is itself a CHANNEL -- an 8 mm web recessed between a 12 mm top and bottom flange on all four sides, where the first build had a plain slab -- and a SINGLE plane falling 2.90 at -Z to 2.40 at +Z. The declared 2.90 is the top of the crests and the crest that sets it is the DEEPENED one at a sheet lap, standing 1.8 amplitudes proud; authored off the ordinary crest it stood at 2.905 and the bay was over its own envelope.
featureReviews.notes: The proxy reads the footprint as rectangular at 0.858:1; the notes fix a square 4 m cell and govern. Everything under the sheet now hangs from the underside of its TROUGHS rather than its mean plane, so the beam's top flange and the purlins no longer stand 18 and 3 mm up into the corrugation valleys and show through them.

Measured on MATCHED WINDOWS entirely inside the deck -- plate 280..760 x 150..300 (n 72,000), render 300..720 x 280..420 (n 58,800) -- the plate reads mean 187.8, sd 26.1, p05 144.0, p50 187.4, p95 229.2 and the shipped deck reads mean 196.8, sd 22.3, p05 151.3, p50 201.9, p95 221.6 -- 85% of the plate's spread. The first build read 193.7 / 195.6 / 227.8 at saturation 0.007 to 0.021: the right tone and effectively one colour.
featureReviews.notes: 2,516 triangles for the deck and 3,188 for the bay, against the registry notes' prediction that modelled flutes would eat the whole budget. The canvas ripple is phase-locked to the geometry at 13 per metre in both, with a trough at x = 0 in both.

featureReviews.evidence: Channel section built as a web and two flanges per post with the WEB darker than the flanges it sits between (the plate's #5c2c28 against #78342e, about 0.79 in linear terms; the first build had it the brighter of the two and a channel read as a bar). BOTH materials are envelope re-based, so a chalk bloom can land brighter than the clean tone a multiply could only darken. Measured over the POSTS ALONE -- the rows below the beam soffit, where nothing up-facing is in frame -- the front view runs mean 51.5, p05 44.2, p50 49.0, p95 68.2 and the back view mean 38.8, p05 31.0, p50 35.1, p95 55.6, against a plate whose posts sit at 28.6, 38.7, 54.1, 66.0, 67.4 and 72.0. The first build rendered three separate posts and every face of them at exactly #a33123, luma 72.2.
featureReviews.notes: The world UV scale is set by the post and not chosen: at 0.80 m a 0.12 m post crossed 15% of one tile and every post crossed the same 15%; at 0.40 m the strip repeated six times down each post as a chevron ladder; at 1.10 m it is two repeats and the y tint carries the rest.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.94. 3,188/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. Turntable passes at every azimuth with holed=false and an enclosed-background fraction of 0.0005 to 0.0074 against the gate ceiling of 0.01, so it is run WITHOUT --allow-holes.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three spec components on two materials plus one repetition system: the bolt heads are merged into the frame geometry and the 26 screw washers are one InstancedMesh, so 3 DRAW CALLS of 4.

materials.note: steel and zinc: 2 of 3. Web, flange, beam, bolt and washer are vertex multipliers on one re-based steel envelope; the deck's zoning, course tones and edge rust are vertex multipliers on one re-based zinc envelope.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,188 of 4,000: 360 in the frame merge (30 boxes -- 12 post, 12 beam, 2 purlin, 4 bolt), 2,516 in the corrugated height grid (2,080 in the two 104 x 5 surfaces and 436 in the wound edge strips, which ARE the fluted eave and rake), and 312 in the 26 screw washers. The registry notes predicted modelled flutes would eat the whole budget; measured, the deck is 63% of it and the bay 80%.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes throughout the frame, six rotated onto the 7.1 degree fall; the deck is a height grid with thickness at explicit z stations; the washers are one instanced box.
One InstancedMesh of 26 screw washers. In a scene the HOST places whole bays on the 4 m grid; butted along the fall they step 0.50 m, butted across it they continue one plane.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Both materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px canvases after construction, ~2 MB of texture VRAM, both bound as map AND bump and both drawn in absolute multiplier space over a re-based envelope so a mark may land either side of clean.

risks.description: The registry notes ask for a flat deck with a normal map and say modelled corrugations would eat the whole triangle budget.
risks.mitigation: The cost claim was measured, not assumed: the deck is 2,516 triangles and the bay 3,188 of 4,000. What the notes are right about is that a normal map carries the ripple; what it cannot carry is the fluted eave and rake, which is what a corrugated roof is read by -- the same argument the bamboo module's own notes make for its scalloped eave. The canvas is still bound, as a bump map over the modelled flutes. Recorded in assumptions and depthRationale.

risks.description: The deck is up-facing, where the harness transfer has a large additive term, so a galvanised grey authored at its measured value renders blown -- 241 on the very first build and still 228 at the lit slope on the second.
risks.mitigation: The clean zinc is authored well below the plate, and the SPREAD rather than the level is what was added. Matched windows entirely inside the deck: plate mean 187.8 sd 26.1 p05 144.0 p95 229.2, shipped mean 196.8 sd 22.3 p05 151.3 p95 221.6. The remaining 9 levels of mean are the turntable gate and were measured, not conceded: 4% darker is closer on every statistic and holes at two azimuths.

risks.description: Red oxide measures 28.6 to 72.0 luma on the plate, and giving the frame that whole range puts its median BELOW the backdrop's 58 at three of the four azimuths.
risks.mitigation: The chroma is what carries it, not the luma. The frame is saturation 0.44 to 0.81 throughout, so a post at 30 luma is still about 54 away from the backdrop in RGB, and the turntable gate passes at every azimuth with holed=false -- no --allow-holes, measured after the darkening rather than assumed to survive it.

risks.description: Both surfaces are large against their tiles -- 4 m of deck on a 1 m tile, 3.94 m of beam and 2.4 m of post on a 1.10 m tile -- so any canvas mark of a useful size repeats visibly. Two builds of this pass drew exactly that: a 4 x 4 lattice of chalk blooms across the roof, and thirteen identical pale dots along the fascia.
risks.mitigation: The broad marks were moved OFF the canvas and onto the vertex grid, which spans each surface once; the tile keeps only marks small enough that their repeat reads as grain. The scales are set from the geometry rather than chosen -- 1.00 m to phase-lock the deck's flutes, 1.10 m to hold a post to two vertical repeats.
